label: input token g at original positions 5-8
explanation: Fires when the input is the letter g during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase at position 5 or later (t = 5..8). It fires on essentially every such g, whether or not g appeared earlier. It never fires on g at positions 0-4, at the delimiter, or in the copy phase (including when g is fed back or output), and almost never on other tokens (8 tiny activations under 0.02 of max on t/m/x/2 at t=8). Magnitude grows with position: about 0.2-0.3 of max at t=5, about 0.55-0.65 at t=6-7, and about 0.8-1.0 at t=8. Neighbouring tokens, first token, and digit count have no visible effect.

issues: No systematic counterexamples. On test, 7 steps fire outside the predicate. All of them are at t=8 on non-g tokens (t, d, y, c, v), each at 0.01-0.02 of max, and together they carry 0.0% of the activation mass. There are 0 false positives.

The profile matches every factual claim. Activation is zero in the delimiter and copy phases and zero at t=0-4. At orig_idx 5-8 the firing rate is about 0.034, which equals the base rate of g, so the feature fires on essentially every g there. Magnitude rises with position: the top examples are all g at t=8 near max, the lowest quartile is g at t=5 around 0.2, and repeat g's (e.g. 0.25 then 0.57) still fire. Neighbouring tokens, first token and digit count show flat lift.

Minor caveat: the L and to_go breakdowns are fully explained by the position dependence, because only sequences with L>=6 have positions 5-8. The label 'positions 5-8' is accurate, since the sequence length tops out at 9.
